citations.assessment: The exact aphorism appears at Orlah 1:3:11, embedded in a discussion about grafted plants and the direction of their leaves. The text names Yudan bar Chanin.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: The precise named witness is currently numbered 2:5:2. It has Yudan beRabbi Chanan in a different legal context. This confirms the Chanan spelling but does not equate the people across passages.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: The precise Sanhedrin passage at 10:1:14 has Rabbi Yudan bar Chanan in Rabbi Berekhiah’s name. Preserve the received halakhah number and the difference from Orlah’s Chanin form.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

notes.text: The received numbers remain visible. The checked Orlah, Kiddushin and Sanhedrin place the passages at 1:3:11, 2:5:2 and 10:1:14 respectively. Chanin, beRabbi Chanan and bar Chanan remain local forms.
